Anya — thanks for the clear list. High level plan below (we'll follow up with docs and a short call if helpful):

1) Legal mechanisms we propose
- EU -> US / intra-EU: Standard EU SCCs (module-based execution) as baseline; where customers require additional UK coverage we'll pair SCCs with the UK IDTA addendum.
- For targeted technical measures (logs/audit, retention, SSE) we'll ship a tailored TIA / DTIA artifact that describes the operational controls mapped to the SCC clauses.

2) Subprocessors
- Attached is our current subprocessor matrix (v3). Key entries: cloud infra (shared with other customers), analytics pipeline, and monitoring vendors. We mark which subprocessors process EU-origin data and whether they are within EU regions.
- We can accept a limited EU-processing constraint via a contract clause and routing policy; depends on which features you enable (some batch analytics run in us-east for capacity reasons).

3) Timeline (proposed)
- 2027-05-06: Redwood initial redline of your annotated SCCs + draft UK addendum language
- 2027-05-10: Draft TIA/DTIA + subprocessor SOPs (for procurement review)
- 2027-05-14: Exchange final SCCs/IDTA + legal sign-off target (we can route DocuSign envelope)

4) Asks from Globex (to speed approvals)
- Confirm whether an EU-only processing mandate is absolute or a preference (we can document fallback processing models).
- Confirm procurement's required vendor risk assessment fields so we populate them in the vendor package.

Attachments in this thread: Redwood-proposed-TIA-v1.docx, subprocessor-matrix-v3.csv.

I'll loop in Product Security (cc'd Karhtik) and Legal (Laura) for the redline work. If procurement wants a short 20-min call, happy to set one up.

Priyom / team — quick notes from Product Security:

- We should gate any promise of EU-only processing by feature. For real-time inference we can pin to EU regions; background analytics (aggregates/metrics) currently use a multi-region pipeline and would require masking/aggregation to avoid raw EU PII movement.
- Suggest adding a short clause in the TIA that prohibits non-EU processing of raw EU personal data unless explicit written consent is obtained from the customer. That gives procurement a legal lever while we keep flexibility operationally.
- For the SCC redline: we prefer using the subset of Globex annotations but will propose an opt-in data-at-rest encryption commitment for EU customers (we'll include a performance SLA note).
